question: Can a conservative coarse Richards system with dynamic layer storage but algebraic interface hydraulic potentials and fluxes supply a physically distinct propagation closure without prescribing an arbitrary within-layer transient profile?

candidate_system.dynamic_state: one retained integrated storage S_i per coarse layer
candidate_system.representative_hydraulic_state: If no additional shape state is admitted, a representative psi_i can only be obtained from the retained layer storage and the frozen retention relation.
candidate_system.algebraic_face_variables: one hydraulic trace lambda_j and one conservative flux q_j per layer face
candidate_system.interface_contract: Each internal face has one shared q_j used with opposite signs in the two neighboring storage balances.
candidate_system.intended_property: local and global water conservation without making the face trace or flux a new dynamic memory state

degree_count.conclusion: The algebraic count is square only after a local half-cell hydraulic relation has been selected. Hybridization itself does not provide that relation.

linear_or_frozen_half_cell.derivation: Using a representative K_i(S_i) and a one-sided Darcy drop over d_i/2 on both sides of an internal face, elimination of lambda_j gives q_j = Delta H / [d_i/(2 K_i) + d_(i+1)/(2 K_(i+1))] up to the frozen sign convention.
linear_or_frozen_half_cell.consequence: This is a standard conservative two-point resistance/flux operator. The explicit trace is a numerical hybridization variable, not new hydrological information.
linear_or_frozen_half_cell.repository_relation: It remains in the existing-state coarse Darcy/two-point operator class already interrogated by CURRENT_LAYER_FACE, C4H-C4O and the same-partition coarse-Richards comparator; it is not a new physical reduction family.

nonlinear_steady_half_cell.derivation: If each center-to-face relation is replaced by the exact local steady Darcian integral, the shared interface q_j connects the two representative layer states by one constant steady center-to-center flux.
nonlinear_steady_half_cell.consequence: Static condensation is the DSE2P closure object.
nonlinear_steady_half_cell.repository_relation: DSE2P failed prospective response-free numerical qualification in C5T; reopening its branch, quadrature or bracket after exposure is not authorized.

affine_within_layer_flux.derivation: If transient storage is represented by an affine q(z), continuity gives a spatially uniform dtheta/dt in the layer.
affine_within_layer_flux.consequence: This is the P0 uniform-storage-tendency SCAFP choice derived in C5V.
affine_within_layer_flux.repository_relation: P0 failed its prospective response-free admissibility/existence contract in C5W; interface traces do not change that closure identity.

higher_order_flux_or_nonuniform_storage_.derivation: Any non-affine q(z) introduces additional unresolved divergence/tendency structure. Storage conservation fixes only the integral q_top-q_bottom, not its within-layer distribution.
higher_order_flux_or_nonuniform_storage_.consequence: A new subgrid profile/tendency principle or an additional state is required.
higher_order_flux_or_nonuniform_storage_.repository_relation: This is exactly the underdetermination identified in C5V/C5X. C5Y supplied the first conservation-derived shape state; C5Z rejected only its all-layer cubic-theta reconstruction, not the first moment itself.

dynamic_flux_state.derivation: Richards-Darcy treats q as algebraically related to hydraulic state and gradient; it supplies no independent flux-inertia evolution equation.
dynamic_flux_state.consequence: Promoting q_j to a dynamic memory state would require additional physics or a separately derived reduced-memory law.

conservation_and_dissipation.conservation: A single shared face flux is sufficient to make the coarse storage balances exactly conservative.
conservation_and_dissipation.insufficiency: Conservation does not identify how the unresolved hydraulic drop or storage tendency is distributed inside a coarse layer.
conservation_and_dissipation.dissipation: A minimum-resistance or steady dissipation construction with fixed endpoint hydraulic states collapses to the steady Darcian route; it does not create a transient subgrid storage law from S_i alone.
conservation_and_dissipation.conclusion: Conservation plus algebraic interface unknowns is necessary but not sufficient for a physically distinct transient Layer-ROM closure.

corichards_reconciliation.fact: Mixed and mixed-hybrid Richards formulations in the literature use flux and/or trace unknowns to obtain locally conservative discretizations; those variables are numerical unknowns of the Richards discretization rather than additional hydrological state.
corichards_reconciliation.repository_boundary: LARE-CORICHARDS-Q1 already shows that reduced same-partition conventional Richards has no qualified non-equilibrium dynamic common cohort through R12 under the frozen strict numerical authority.
corichards_reconciliation.consequence: Rewriting a coarse Richards discretization in hybrid form does not by itself create a new reduced physical family or bypass Q1.

independent_theory_context.citation: Radu, F.A., Pop, I.S., Knabner, P. (2004), Order of Convergence Estimates for an Euler Implicit, Mixed Finite Element Discretization of Richards' Equation, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 42, 1452-1478.
independent_theory_context.relevance: Lowest-order Raviart-Thomas mixed formulations treat flux as an explicit numerical unknown and provide a convergent conservative Richards discretization.

independent_theory_context.citation: Belfort, B. et al. (2009), An Efficient Lumped Mixed Hybrid Finite Element Formulation for Variably Saturated Groundwater Flow, Vadose Zone Journal.
independent_theory_context.relevance: Mixed-hybrid formulation exposes face/flux variables while preserving the underlying Richards physics; hybridization is a discretization construction, not a new hydrological closure.

independent_theory_context.citation: Belfort/Younes et al. (2009), An easy and efficient combination of the Mixed Finite Element Method and the Method of Lines for the resolution of Richards' Equation, Environmental Modelling & Software 24, 1122-1126.
independent_theory_context.relevance: The method uses mixed-hybrid finite elements with explicit flux degrees of freedom, supporting the distinction between conservative numerical variables and added dynamic physical state.

next_authority.question: Which physically derived mechanism should carry the missing transient subgrid information now that algebraic interface variables alone reduce to already-closed two-point, DSE2P or P0 closures?
admissible_classes_for_future_read_only_: A realizability-preserving moment/state closure that does not reopen the rejected C5Z cubic-theta reconstruction.

A genuinely conserved interface-local or dual-control-volume state with its own balance law, provided dimensional value and non-duplication with simple layer refinement are established before response.
A separately justified adaptive/moving-partition representation, kept distinct from fixed-partition closure repair.
excluded_shortcuts: Do not retune C5Z polynomial order, moment range, constitutive domain or numerical tolerances after observing C5Z.
Do not reopen DSE2P or P0 under hybrid-variable terminology.
Do not call a conventional mixed-hybrid coarse Richards discretization a new physical ROM family.
Do not add dynamic flux inertia without a physical governing equation.
Do not choose the next family by minimizing exposed C5N/C5P/C5R response error.
